Scottsdale Nightlife Transportation: Hours, Rates and Stops

Scottsdale Sprinters runs Old Town Scottsdale nightlife and bar crawls in a chauffeured party Sprinter booked by the hour — one driver all evening, every stop on the reservation, and the ride home already inside it. The Sprinters lead: the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) seats 16 at $175 an hour, the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) seats 13 at $175 an hour, and the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter seats 15 at $250 an hour. For a bigger group the Party Bus (28 Pax) starts at $1,000 before 8% tax — roughly $36 a seat across its 28 seats — and the Pink Hummer Limo is the one for the photo. Every party unit carries a 4-hour minimum. For 15 people at that minimum, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) works out to about $47 each. Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol; if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on that trip. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

What is Scottsdale nightlife transportation with a driver?

Scottsdale Sprinters books a night out as hours with a chauffeur rather than as separate trips: one vehicle, one driver, and every stop the group lists, across a published minimum of 4 hours. The clock starts at the first pickup and stops at the last drop-off, so the ride home is already inside the booking. A metered ride quotes each leg, and a group of 10 needs several cars per leg, so the ride out, the move between stops and the ride home become three transactions and three chances to split up. An hourly charter is one: the vehicle is yours for the window you booked, and it waits between stops. Because the time is already bought, added stops cost nothing on an hourly charter; a point-to-point transfer is the other product here and charges $50 for each stop beyond pickup and drop-off. What no booking buys is the property's own decision about where a commercial vehicle may stop or wait. The house rules invite you to use the chauffeur for the rest — "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Which vehicle fits a Scottsdale night out by group size?

Scottsdale Sprinters leads a night out with its party Sprinters: the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) seats 16, the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) 13 and the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter 15. The Party Bus (28 Pax) is the largest at 28 seats and $250 an hour, and the Pink Hummer Limo tops the range at $1,180. Seats are published seated capacity — a limit, not a target. Starting total is the published rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's minimum, the arithmetic the checkout runs, and 8% Arizona tax sits on top. Per seat does not follow the rate: the Party Bus (28 Pax) reads $36 a seat because it seats 28, the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) $54 on a lower rate because it seats 13. Nothing on this page is an executive shuttle, and that is deliberate. The occasion pool this service resolves to also carries the executive vehicles as a quiet second ride for a mixed group; a night out is a celebration booking, so these units are the celebration half of it, Sprinters first. What does an Old Town Scottsdale bar crawl cost for 15 people?

Scottsdale Sprinters prices an Old Town Scottsdale bar crawl by the vehicle, not the head. For 15 people at the 4-hour minimum, the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) is $700, about $47 each; the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter is $1,000, about $67 each; the Party Bus (28 Pax) is $1,000, about $67 each. Those shares are the published starting total divided by 15, before 8% Arizona tax. The Pink Hummer Limo seats 18 and is $1,180, about $79 each. Seats are a limit, not a target: the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) seats fewer than 15, so a group this size either splits across two vehicles or moves up to one that seats everyone. How the crawl works: book the hours, not the bars. One pickup address, every stop listed on the reservation up front, the chauffeur waiting between them, and the ride home already inside the booking. On an hourly charter the second and third stops cost nothing; hours past the minimum bill at the same rate. Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol, if anyone under 21 rides no alcohol comes on that trip, and the full house rules are quoted below.

How does Scottsdale Sprinters run a night out in Old Town Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters runs an Old Town Scottsdale night as a block of hours with a named list of stops on the reservation. A 7-hour booking bills 6 hours rather than 7: the published ladder gives back 1 hour once a booking reaches 7. Build the evening backwards: pick the hour the group wants to be home, count back through the stops, and that is the window to book. On the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) a 7-hour night bills 6 hours at $175 an hour — $1,050 before tax, about $66 a seat with 16 aboard. The same night on the Party Bus (28 Pax) is $1,500, about $54 a seat with 28. The stop list is the part groups underuse. What costs a night is never the second or third stop — those are free on an hourly charter — it is the stop nobody wrote down. Pickup is a street address rather than a zone, and a 28-seat unit needs room to stand, turn and reload, so a named cross street beats a driveway.

How does Scottsdale Sprinters handle a concert or a game night?

Scottsdale Sprinters treats a concert or a game night as the same hourly booking as any other night out, run to Phoenix, Glendale and Tempe instead of staying in Scottsdale. One vehicle holds 10 or more people together through a post-event crowd, and the clock covers the wait because the wait is inside the hours you booked. This is where an hourly charter separates from anything metered. After an event every car in the area leaves at once, and the group that arrived together is the likeliest to lose each other. A charter is one published hourly rate, agreed in writing. Published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley, so a night that starts in one city and ends in another is still one charter. What is never promised is a curb. Event traffic plans are set by the property, change between events, and are enforced on the night by people who have never seen your reservation. What the reservations desk can keep is a written pickup point agreed before you travel, one group contact reachable afterwards, and a chauffeur who moves to wherever the vehicle may wait.

What is included in a Scottsdale night-out booking, and what is not?

A chauffeur, the vehicle for the hours you booked, and bottled water are what a Scottsdale Sprinters night includes. One page of house rules governs every trip whatever the vehicle, and 3 of those rules carry a stated fee — the largest being $1,500 for smoking or vaping of any kind. Drinking on board is allowed as the house rules state it and not beyond: "Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol, and we do not sell it. Arizona vehicle-for-hire open-container policy, A.R.S. § 4-251, allows it, and if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on that trip." On its limit: "No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks." And the rule people are most often surprised by — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." Extras are add-ons, and alcohol is never one of them. In the owner's words: "Add-ons include decorations of every kind, custom signs, a custom AI song, non-alcoholic refreshments, premium Fiji water and most custom touches a limo can offer." Three carry a fee, and each says why. "No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee." ($1,500). "Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee." ($450). And the one nobody plans for: "If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves." ($450). Condition is documented rather than argued about at two in the morning. "Before every trip your chauffeur takes a documented set of photos of the interior. They are for our internal records only." "You authorize us to charge the card on file for damage beyond normal use. We will never charge for damage without telling you first, with the photos, so there are no surprises."

What does a Scottsdale night out cost, and how do you reserve one?

A night out starts at $700 — $175 an hour across the 4-hour minimum on the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) — before 8% tax, and $1,000 on the Party Bus (28 Pax), which carries 28. Reserve online, or call or text (623) 986-6339. The arithmetic is the same for every unit and there is nothing else in it: the published hourly rate times your billable hours, plus 8% Arizona tax. No booking fee, no fuel fee, no per-mile charge, and no different rate for a midnight hour than a six o'clock one. Gratuity is optional. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums, and they are what the booking flow charges against. Payment follows the published deposit policy: pay 50% today by card and the balance is charged to that saved card 48 hours before pickup, or pay in full at checkout. To reserve, choose the vehicle, set the date, time and hours, add every stop, and confirm. Availability is specific to a date and a vehicle, so request a current quote with your date, hours and group size.
